subject: Post-demo recap: procurement route & marketplace interest
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: procurement route & marketplace interest

Thanks again for your time today, Sofia — appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of ask/fit
- Primary use case: patient triage & summarization for inbound clinical messages
- Target latency & throughput: soft SLO 200ms median, spikes to 800ms for long threads
- Data residency: US-only, SOC2 + HIPAA alignment required

Procurement signals you raised
- Procurement prefers either a PO (net 30/45) or AWS Marketplace private offer for financing and consolidated billing
- Security team will request audit logs and KMS/HSM details
- RFP with questions coming from procurement — you mentioned a spreadsheet will arrive by end of week

Proposed seller-side actions
1) Share a short RFP Q&A template for procurement to speed review (attached stub).
2) Prepare a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) outlining milestones for procurement, legal, and security (I’ll attach a draft by Friday).
3) We’ll confirm Marketplace private offer capabilities vs PO billing with finance and provide an estimate of timing for a Private Offer setup (typical 2–3 weeks once PO terms are agreed).

Can you confirm whether procurement prefers a Marketplace private offer as the default path, or should we plan for a PO-first approach? If PO-first, do you have a preferred payment term (net 30 vs net 45) and a PO contact we should loop in now?

Attachments: Lumina_RFP_QA.xlsx (spreadsheet) — lightweight Q&A template to start.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the MAP draft and a short note from our finance team on marketplace timelines.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sofia Martin <sofia.martin@luminahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@luminahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement route & marketplace interest

Thanks, Mina — good recap. A couple quick clarifications from procurement side:

- Procurement leaning: likely want PO-first for initial pilot (institutional approval seems simpler via our standard PO workflow). We are open to later migrating to AWS Marketplace Private Offer for enterprise rollout, but the pilot needs to move quickly.
- Payment terms: usually net 30; we can push to net 45 with justification but prefer net 30.
- PO contact: Rebecca Chen (rebecca.chen@luminahealth.com) — I’ve cc’d procurement alias above to ensure visibility.
- Security asks: our InfoSec will ask for SOC 2 Type II report, data retention policy, and evidence of key management practices (KMS/HSM). Please include links or docs in the MAP.

I’ll share the formal RFP spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow — it includes a short section on preferred billing route and legal standard terms. For the MAP, please include an estimated procurement/legal timeline so we can align expectations.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — one ask: can Redwood provide a short note on how migrating from PO to AWS Marketplace private offer typically impacts billing cadence and invoicing for finance teams? That’ll help our FP&A team understand the downstream impact.

Regards,
Sofia
Sofia Martin
Director of Product Operations | Lumina Health
sofia.martin@luminahealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 10:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement route & marketplace interest

Quick note from engineering/solutions:
- From a technical standpoint there’s no functional difference in how the service runs between Marketplace private offer and direct PO billing — runtimes, latency, and SLOs are unchanged.
- Marketplace private offers add a small onboarding step on our side (1–2 business days to configure entitlements) and typically require finance to accept consolidated Marketplace invoices; we can provide a short 1-page explainer for FP&A.
- For the audit pieces: I’ve attached a checklist stub we normally send to InfoSec that maps required artifacts (SOC2 report, KMS details, pen test summary) to our documentation links.

Happy to join a quick call with Rebecca and your procurement team to walk through the MAP and the FP&A note.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
